reviews.title: Sadly too many glitches and poor customer service.
reviews.text:
I used Speechify for a year during my postgraduate studies but then got very frustrated with the glitches that were just never dealt with. On describing the glitches several times to the team, there was never any reply or attempt to work on those. I use a Mac with the newest system update, so I believe many other users have similar issues.
It has some great features but apparently not very willing staff behind it to have a good relationship with their customers.
The price for the app is way too high, considering all those aspects.
This is sad, as the app really has potential.
There are very good alternative apps which do a better job than Speechify for a similar or lower price.

I would be happy to re-evaluate my feedback once I see a real effort to work on these glitches and improve the customer service.

reviews.title: 😡 False advertisement
reviews.text:
When I first tried Speechify, I was genuinely impressed by the free version. I loved that I could scan a book I already owned and turn it into a podcast. However, I could only listen to two chapters before having to pay to continue using the podcast feature. After some time away, I decided to give it another shot with a new book I purchased, hoping for a fresh podcast experience. There was a $25 one-time lifetime deal, so I grabbed it, expecting it to be similar to what I had before—perhaps with exciting new features like celebrity voices, as advertised. Sadly, the AI podcast feature for books seems to have vanished; I even took a picture of my new book, eager to listen to it, but there’s no way to use this feature anymore. 
After searching through the app, I discovered a paywall that requires a $139-a-year plan to use the podcast feature and the voices. That wasn’t stated when I purchased the $25 lifetime feature; I thought I was getting the voices, the podcast, and all the features for that price. It is a very misleading and deceptive practice to lure people in.
In less than 25 minutes on the paid plan, I’m already so disappointed that I'm considering calling Apple for a refund.
***Update***
🤔 Now I don’t see the Lifetime $25 one-time payment option I paid for available anymore.

reviews.title: Will ram upselling down your throat from the moment you sign up.
reviews.text:
Downloaded Speechify and Eleven Reader to compare side by side. 

Eleven Reader has a pay month by month subscription. Have been using it for a week and really like it. And you get a week free trial which is long enough to see if you like it. 

Speechify give you 3 days free. And will start pushing you to upgrade from the second you start using it.  
And they only offer a year subscription. 

Firstly I’m not going to commit to a year subscription after only 3 days of trialling it. 

Second, why would you push people to upgrade the moment they start using it? Who is going to choose to pay to subscribe for a year after 10 seconds into using an app. 

This isn’t going to encourage people to upgrade or subscribe!
It makes you look pushy and desperate. 

I immediately got a bad impression of the company due to the constant upselling to the point I didn’t even trust them to want to try the 3 day period as they literally screamed the type of company where you will end the free trial and opt to not subscribe and will bill you anyway. You then spend weeks fighting to get a refund for a subscription you didn’t want. 

It’s a shame as the app may actually be quite good. But I found Eleven Reader gave me what I will need and didn’t have enough faith in Speechify to even want to risk giving them my card details. 

It may have been better than Eleven reader for all I know.  

But until you stop the aggressive upselling, give users more than 3 days to trial it (I do have work and a life) 3

reviews.title: Please less payment, so much money spent then wasted
reviews.text:
I just recently bought this app and i really thought that I found a good app that would help me start feeling like I wanted to read. So and anyone who really wants this app would, I paid the 14 dollars for it and I’m perfectly fine with it.
Then I found a book and I could only listen to 30 minutes of it before I have to pay; i was like ok not too too bad I’ll just only listen to 30 minutes now and pay later. Then I  start listening to the book…and the voice was horrid absolutely horrid, so I go and try to change the voice to the founders voice because I liked that one. But it costed more money, like I don’t truly want to be spending $145 a year so I can use the app that i already paid for. So then I’m like whatever I’ll just listen with this voice. Then every single time there is a period, it says dot, do you know how annoying that gets with you have really bad adhd and just want to read a book without getting lost every paragraph, and I thought this app was made to help with that. But it does the opposite. I would only recommend this app to people that are willing to pay a lot more then they should probably be paying to get help with what the app was basically ment to help. Would not recommend and if possible please add another free humanoid voice.

reviews.title: Expensive
reviews.text: I have had enough of these so called ‘free’ apps with shorter and shorter free trials. Here it’s only 3 days. No mention of freedom to cancel. This omission should be taken as an alarm. We live in an increasingly soulless society. A billionaire said that if he could cover the sky and charge people to see the stars he would. Today I’m afraid nobody wants to look at the stars anymore. That way God and the old spirit of man resides. Science has freed humanity or so humanity is told. Freedom itself is a word almost lost. The drug dealer gets his customers by offering his opiates free then cheap and then barely affordable. I am old enough to remember it all. Free app still remind my generation of what that word meant. When we are gone the word free will go with us.

reviews.title: IMO: Too focused on AI features to provide support for the software’s basic function.
reviews.text:
I used this app for 4 years during my undergraduate and it helped me out a bunch. Back then it cost $50/year. Now it cost $150/year and the user interface is 100x better. But now the app doesn’t work half the time. I’ll spend 40 minutes taking pictures of text and cropping it all. Then when I hit the play button all it does is read 1 sentence then buffer for 2 minutes. I have listened to 161 hours of content using this app so I am very familiar with it. It’s great if it work. I hope they fix whatever is wrong but right now it’s costing me a lot of time at work since I have a reading disability and the one service that helps doesn’t work half the time. Wish I could give this 5 stars. Maybe I’ll change the review is they fix their problems. Feels liked hey are putting more resources into their new AI features than just making sure the basic function of the software works.

Update:
They just keep making it worse. The scan feature is worse now than it’s ever been. I read about 300 pages a week using speechify because it’s the only service like it I know of. I spend about 4+ hours every Sunday scanning those pages. Now because they have changed the scam feature that time is going to double because it’s not intuitive and they deleted about half the features.

reviews.title: DON’T BE FOOLED!
reviews.text:
Their social ads make it look like you can just scan the cover of any book & it will ready it to you. This is not the case. You have to spend hours taking pictures of each individual page. Which was ok albeit a bit of a waste of time. However, since the last update you can’t even do this properly.

I’ve now tried to scan the same chapter of my text book 4 times now. The app either crashes mid scan & you have to start the process again from the beginning or it completes the scan but then jumbles all of the pages up basically rendering the scan completely useless anyway!

Save yourself the time and money & don’t bother! You can’t even pay monthly. The annual payment should have been for first Red Flag to be honest.

reviews.title: Safe, non-confrontational selections. Very vanilla book selections
reviews.text:
I have two very long books that I have started that I was hoping to be able to finish with this app. I drive out of town frequently and was going to use that time on the road more productively, but this app didn’t recognize or have access to either of my books. One of these books was written by a New York Times best selling Author Annie Jacobsen. The book title was titled “Operation Paperclip”.
The second book title was “To the Victor go the myths and Monuments”. By Arther Thompson. 
Due to how narrow of selections that seem to be available, I will be cancelling my subscription before the trial period ends. 
In an age where freedom of speech is under attack, and  tools of social engineering, shadow banning, historical facts are edited like life is a fictional play that you can just change any time your personal security or point of view is proven invalid or becomes threatened, I was hoping that this would be a useful tool for me to finish these very important books written by historical investigative journalists pointing out a great divergence between public school text book history, and documented Library of Congress recorded historical facts. 
This app appears to be just another safe, non-controversial, vanilla, and controlled 1984’esque platform, that furthers the nanny state by removing anything that would threaten the image of government, its officials, and some of the filthy and criminal actions they have perpetrated on the world.
